observations.semantic_recognizability: v006 reads as a compact workshop assembly table in the Room B production render.
observations.silhouette_quality: The lower 24-inch height and broad 32-inch depth distinguish it from the elevated workbench; the top and legs remain plain compared with the concept.
observations.proportion: The GLB measures exactly 42 x 24 x 32 inches and preserves the room’s height/depth relationship.
observations.geometric_detail: Dog holes, breadboard ends, a drawer, tapered legs, lower stretchers and a side vise are modeled, though several details are obscured in the room capture.
observations.material_realism: The oak and walnut are separated, but the surface reads as flat amber material rather than figured timber.
observations.surface_variation: The detail view shows little board-to-board grain or wear variation.
observations.close_up_quality: Close inspection finds shallow drawer relief and understated joinery; the target shows stronger end grain, rails and fitted joints.
observations.gameplay_readability: The low table shape and single front drawer remain recognizable at normal viewing distance.
observations.scale_fidelity: The validator reports an exact 42 x 24 x 32-inch source envelope.
observations.art_direction_fit: The backend switch improves authored construction, but the finish and medium-scale woodworking detail remain far below the approved target.
observations.technical_integration: Godot 4.7.2 imports the embedded GLB with no issues; the candidate stays review-only because it fails the visual gate.

hard_fail_reasons: The strict visual gate fails for craftsmanship, surface variation, material response and neutral-viewer realism.
defects: Top grain and end-grain boards remain too flat.
Joinery shoulders and drawer relief lack enough depth to read at close range.
The side vise and cup pull are not clearly visible in the available production views.
next_action_hypothesis: Keep the validated 42 x 24 x 32-inch envelope; bring the top closer to the target with distinct board/end-grain pieces, deeper fitted rail joints, readable vise and cup-pull hardware, and stronger per-board grain.
incumbent_comparison: Compared with room_assembly_table-v005, room_assembly_table-v006 is a useful challenger but does not clear the target’s strict transfer gate. The authored joinery is a real geometry improvement; its finish, craft and exact depth need another pass.

neutral_viewer_realism.evidence: room_assembly_table-v006 remains visibly simpler and flatter than its approved target in the registered RoomScale renders.

close_inspection.evidence: The registered detail capture for room_assembly_table-v006 shows shallow construction relief, weak material variation and missing target-level joinery.

edge_treatment.evidence: On room_assembly_table v006, the breadboard corners, tapered feet and drawer rails remain mostly square; the small bevels do not reproduce the approved table’s shaped edges.

joins.evidence: Room_assembly_table v006 has modeled shelf shoulders and frame members, but their shallow relief and simple intersections do not read as fitted joinery at the detail angle.

thickness.evidence: The registered views of room_assembly_table v006 show a substantial top, visible apron and lower frame whose thicknesses look credible for a low assembly bench.

hardware.evidence: The side vise and small drawer button on room_assembly_table v006 are present, but the vise fittings and handle are too understated to read clearly against the target.

material_response.evidence: Room_assembly_table v006 separates oak from walnut, though both surfaces look evenly colored and smoother than the approved workshop reference.

surface_variation.evidence: The close render of room_assembly_table v006 shows little distinct grain across the top boards and no convincing edge wear.

manufacturing_detail.evidence: Room_assembly_table v006 includes dog holes, breadboard ends, a drawer and stretchers, yet the details remain shallow and less deliberate than the reference construction.
